question: A diabetic patient with poorly controlled diabetes presents with proptosis, progressive visual loss, and black necrotic eschar on the nasal mucosa. CT orbit shows orbital apex involvement with intracranial extension. What is the MOST appropriate surgical intervention for the orbital component?

answers.text: Enucleation — removes the globe and reduces orbital volume to limit spread

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Enucleation removes only the globe. In orbital mucormycosis with apex and intracranial extension, much more extensive debridement of all involved orbital and sinus tissue is required to achieve disease control.

answers.text: Evisceration — preserves the sclera to maintain orbital volume for later rehabilitation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Evisceration leaves orbital tissues intact and is wholly insufficient to control invasive fungal infection spreading to the orbital apex and intracranially. It is contraindicated here.

answers.text: Orbital exenteration — removal of all orbital contents to achieve adequate surgical debridement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Exenteration (removal of globe + all orbital soft tissues ± eyelids) combined with systemic antifungals is the life-saving intervention for invasive mucormycosis with orbital extension. The primary goal is survival — cosmesis is secondary.

answers.text: Medical management alone with IV amphotericin B — surgery is deferred until clinical response is assessed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Medical management alone carries unacceptably high mortality when CT shows orbital apex and intracranial involvement. Surgical debridement is essential alongside antifungal therapy. 'Watch-and-wait' is not appropriate here.

overallFeedback.feedback: For invasive mucormycosis: exenteration removes all orbital contents to debulk fungal load; systemic amphotericin B simultaneously. Enucleation/evisceration are inadequate. Early aggressive surgery saves lives.
Correct. Orbital mucormycosis with intracranial extension = exenteration + systemic antifungals. This is a life-threatening emergency.
